text.p: Zannex Securities has raised its rating of Israel's Supersol Ltd to long-term buy from buy-on-weakness in a report released on Wednesday.

"First-half 1997 is going to be a difficult period for Supersol," said analyst Tal Lianai. "The non-food business losses and the Shekem stores will pressure operating and net income. However, we believe (three) factors will strengthen the stock price during the following 12 months"

First, Zannex said, sales revenues per square metre at its newly acquired Shekem stores would gradually rise and second Supersol would probably close its loss-making Super Office supplies business in the second half.
Supersol will also benefit from a planned offering in the U.S. market, raising the company's Tel Aviv-traded stock price, Zannex said.

Liani noted that Supersol is currently traded at a prospective price-to-earnings ratio of 17.6 for 1997, in comparison to the average P/E of around 30 for retail food chains in other emerging markets.
